Verifier notes and special checks

Twenty-six printed regions on one page, in common time with one sharp. The upper staff opens in treble and the lower staff opens in bass, and each later system reprints those same clefs. No clef change, meter change, key change, repeat, or ending is printed. System 2 ends without a barline: its last region and the first region of system 3 are one cadenza split by the system break. That cadenza closes on a thin-thick double bar. The last region is a whole-note bar closed by a thin-thick final barline. The cadenza's longest voice holds eleven and a half quarter-note beats on system 2 and eight and a half quarter-note beats on system 3.

  • System 2, right end of the staff: Does system 2 end with a closing barline? No. The staff lines stop near x 1631 and the gap between the staves is blank, so the last region continues on system 3.
  • System 2, stems under the first fermata: Is the vertical stroke near x 1146 a barline? No. It is the stem of the fermata chord. It does not cross the blank gap between the staves.
  • System 3, end of the cadenza: Is the double bar a repeat? No. A thin stroke at x 763 and a thick stroke at x 768 close the cadenza. No repeat dots are printed.
  • System 4, last region: Which stroke closes the final bar? The thin stroke at x 1626. The thick stroke beside it runs to about x 1644 and has no repeat dots.
